_readme: Targets and p95 latency budgets for scripts/nightly_load_test.py (issue #40), driven by the python-nightly-load-test CI job in ci/python.yml. Each entry in "targets" is one GET endpoint to measure; "budget_p95_ms" on a target overrides "default_budget_p95_ms" below, which overrides the job's LOAD_TEST_DEFAULT_BUDGET_MS variable. Add a target once you have a real endpoint to measure: {"name": "...", "method": "GET", "path": "/your/endpoint/", "budget_p95_ms": <optional>, "note": "why this budget"}. An empty "targets" list is a valid, inert starting state — the CI job prints 'nothing to measure' and exits 0 rather than failing a clone that has not wired up an API yet.
status_note: No target is configured yet because Blueprint ships no application to measure. default_budget_p95_ms below is a documented starting SLO, not a value traced to any measured_p95_ms — see budget_formula. The FIRST real target you add should be measured with --measure-only and given its own budget_p95_ms via the formula; only fall back to default_budget_p95_ms for an endpoint you have not gotten around to measuring yet, and revisit it once you have.
budget_formula: Once you have a real measurement: budget_p95_ms = ceil(measured_p95_ms * 1.4 / 5) * 5 -- a 1.4x factor (a reasonable midpoint of the commonly-used 1.3-1.5x range) rounded up to the nearest 5ms so CI comparisons have a little headroom for cross-run measurement noise without the number itself being invented round. Re-derive per target with --measure-only when its endpoint's implementation changes materially -- never hand-adjust a single budget_p95_ms without a fresh measurement behind it.
default_budget_rationale: 500ms is a conservative, generic p95 ceiling for a single synchronous JSON API GET under CI-scale load -- loose enough that ordinary cross-runner variance will not false-positive the nightly job, tight enough to catch a gross regression (e.g. an N+1 query turning a 50ms lookup into several seconds) before a user feels it. It is a placeholder, not a derived value: replace it, per endpoint, with a real budget_p95_ms computed from --measure-only output using budget_formula above as soon as you have a target worth measuring. Treat a target still relying on this default after its first real nightly run as unfinished configuration, not a passing gate.
